personality_one_liner: A high-contrast, tactical command center designed for instant glanceability and zero-friction broadcast control.

spacing.rule: Dense, tactical spacing for operational surfaces. Whitespace is used only to separate logical component groups. Margins and paddings are tight (sm/md) to maximize glanceability and screen real estate.

do's: Use solid surfaceSecondary and dividers for elevation.
dont's: No blur or glassmorphism. This is a high-performance utility app where clarity beats aesthetics.

screens.name: Home / Mode Selector
screens.purpose: Launchpad to select the operational mode (OBS Tally, Autonomous Studio, or Alarm System).
screens.layout: Grid of massive tactile blocks (width: 100% of row, or 2-col flex wrap). Each block has an icon and heavy Barlow Condensed typography. A subtle background image with vertical gradient scrim sits behind the cards to provide a studio feel.

screens.name: OBS Connection Screen
screens.purpose: Configure WebSocket connection to OBS and assign the device to a scene/source.

states.empty: No scenes found. Check OBS connection.
states.error: Connection failed banner (red surface, white text) with a 'Retry' button.

screens.layout: Top section: IP/Port/Password form with solid inputs (surfaceTertiary) and labels above. Middle: Sticky connection status indicator. Bottom: Scrollable list of available OBS sources/scenes. Use single-column layout.

screens.name: Tally Light (Fullscreen)
screens.purpose: A massive, room-scale visual indicator for the camera operator.

states.loading: Black screen with 'WAITING FOR SIGNAL' text.

screens.layout: Completely immersive. Hide navigation if possible, or use a floating dismiss button. Idle = Pure black surface (surface) with dimmed grey text. PREVIEW = Fullscreen 'success' (#00E676) background with massive black typography. LIVE = Fullscreen 'error' (#FF3333) background with massive white typography. Source name is vertically and horizontally centered.

screens.name: Director Control Panel
screens.purpose: Autonomous mode central dashboard to see and control all connected phones/cameras.

states.empty: Dotted border container: 'No cameras joined session.' + Share Code CTA.

screens.layout: Multi-column grid of camera tiles. Each tile shows camera name, current state (border color: green/red/grey). Tapping a tile toggles its state (Preview -> Live). Bottom fixed area: 'Kill All' or 'Blackout' master CTA.

screens.name: Alarm Sender / Dashboard
screens.purpose: A tactile panic-button interface to alert the autonomous tally screens.
screens.layout: Massive central 'CALL' or 'ALERT' circular button (using brandPrimary or error color), surrounded by 3-4 preset message chips ('Need coffee', 'Quiet please').

screens.name: Incoming Alert (Receiver)
screens.purpose: Fullscreen interruptive visual/audio alarm triggered by the sender.
screens.layout: Flashing fullscreen state. Oversized message text. Huge 'DISMISS' swipe-to-acknowledge or hold-to-acknowledge button at the bottom.

hero_studio.alt: Audio mixing console with illuminated buttons

hero_lens.alt: Close up of a camera lens

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly follow the Dark-First Utility DARK guidelines. The app must feel like professional hardware, not a consumer social app.
Borders and backgrounds dictate hierarchy. Use solid surface colors and dividers. DO NOT use glassmorphism, blur, or heavy drop shadows.
Typography is critical: Use Barlow Condensed for all metrics, state indicators, and large text. Use IBM Plex Sans for forms, settings, and smaller metadata. Ensure maximum WCAG AA contrast.

Tally Logic: Map semantic colors strictly -> `error` (#FF3333) is always used for LIVE / ON-AIR states. `success` (#00E676) is always used for PREVIEW / STANDBY states. Idle states use `surface` pure black.
The Fullscreen Tally and Alert Receiver screens MUST force the screen to stay awake (`expo-keep-awake`).
On the Director Control Panel, cameras are represented by tiles. The tile's border color should reflect the camera's current state (Red for live, Green for preview).
Use tactile feedback (haptics) on every interaction, especially for mode selection and tally state toggling. Wire it on the press events.
Never use indigo, blue, purple, or generic app colors. Stick strictly to the defined obsidian/slate base, amber brand, and broadcast red/green.
